claims.source_locator: Manual PDF pp. 43-44 and 47 (printed pp. 40-41 and 44): stable eGFR risk evidence and prophylaxis indications
claims.fact: Stable eGFR 45 or greater is not an independent nephrotoxic risk factor; routine prophylaxis is not indicated for stable eGFR 30 or greater, while eGFR 30-44 may be considered individually only in high-risk circumstances.

claims.source_locator: Manual PDF pp. 44-46 (printed pp. 41-43): AKI threshold unreliability, caution, standard diagnostic dose, volume expansion, and prophylaxis
claims.fact: For AKI, no serum creatinine or eGFR threshold adequately stratifies risk because serum creatinine is unreliable. AKI or stable eGFR below 30 enters the higher-risk pathway; use isotonic volume expansion when appropriate, prefer normal saline, recognize the ideal regimen is unknown, assess volume tolerance, and do not underdose diagnostic IV contrast solely to mitigate CI-AKI risk.

claims.source_locator: Manual PDF p. 47 (printed p. 44): anuric dialysis and residual renal function
claims.fact: Anuric end-stage kidney disease without a functioning transplant has no further renal injury to prevent, while dialysis patients with residual urine output should be treated as higher risk for loss of residual function.

claims.source_locator: Manual PDF p. 35 (printed p. 32): warming recommendations and limited evidence grades
claims.fact: Routine warming is not recommended for lower-viscosity iodinated agents; higher-viscosity warming may be considered selectively to reduce viscosity or injection pressure but is not a routine requirement.

claims.source_locator: Introduction and Table 1 note: age, screening, known-primary-cancer, and immunocompromise exclusions
claims.fact: The table is limited to eligible incidental nodules in adults at least 35 years old; screening, immunocompromise, known primary cancer, younger age, and uncertain eligibility route away without a Fleischner schedule.

claims.source_locator: General Recommendations and Figures 1-5; Perifissural Nodules section
claims.fact: Table use requires adequate thin-section characterization; definitively benign fat or calcification and typical intrapulmonary-lymph-node morphology route away without an unnecessary surveillance schedule.

claims.source_locator: Table 1 solid section, journal page 230; Recommendations 1-2
claims.fact: The solid pathways preserve every single and multiple 5, 6, 8, and 9 mm low/high-risk boundary vector, including the table's distinct optional and required later CT language.

claims.source_locator: Recommendation 2: at least one nodule at least 6 mm and larger-or-more-suspicious solitary-path routing; Recommendation 5: most-suspicious-nodule routing
claims.fact: Multiple-nodule table selection uses whether any nodule reaches 6 mm, separately records the dominant most-suspicious nodule, applies the solitary pathway when a larger or more suspicious dominant solid nodule requires it, and distinguishes cohort persistence from interval evolution in the management-driving nodule(s).

claims.source_locator: Table 1 subsolid section, journal page 230; Recommendations 3-5 and interval-growth examples
claims.fact: Subsolid management distinguishes baseline persistence checks from persistent surveillance and established interval evolution: pure-ground-glass growth is not returned to a baseline schedule, new solid transformation routes to part-solid evaluation, and multiple persistent nodules follow the applicable 2/4-year or most-suspicious-nodule pathway.

claims.source_locator: Recommendations 3-4: selected suspicious pure-ground-glass or part-solid nodules close to 6 mm
claims.fact: The selected close-to-6-mm option applies to both pure ground-glass and part-solid nodules and permits consideration of CT at 2 and 4 years without demanding an unreliable component measurement in a sub-6-mm part-solid nodule.

claims.source_locator: Recommendation 4: baseline persistence assessment; persistent component thresholds; growth, suspicious morphology, or component larger than 8 mm escalation
claims.fact: For solitary part-solid nodules at least 6 mm, baseline imaging first assesses persistence, persistent stable components below 6 mm enter annual follow-up for at least 5 years, persistent components at least 6 mm are highly suspicious, and a growing component, particularly suspicious morphology, or component larger than 8 mm triggers diagnostic evaluation options.

claims.source_locator: Risk Factors for Malignancy and Risk Estimation and Risk Models; Table 1 solid risk columns
claims.fact: Solid-nodule low risk is below 5% and high risk combines the ACCP intermediate and high categories at 5% or greater; the clinician selects the holistic category rather than the tool inferring it from one factor.

claims.source_locator: Measurement recommendations and Figures 1-4 and 12-17: small-nodule average, at-least-10-mm two-axis record, largest solid component, lung windows, and established size change
claims.fact: Use lung windows and whole millimeters; average orthogonal diameters; record both axes at ≥10 mm and for part-solid geometry; separately record the largest solid-component long axis. A component may exceed the rounded average, never the actual overall long axis. Linear growth requires ≥2 mm average-diameter change on comparable CT; validated volumetry follows its reproducibility protocol.

claims.source_locator: Measurement statement Figure 6: nodules 3 mm or smaller should not be measured
claims.fact: Nodules 3 mm or smaller use a categorical very-small pathway instead of a false-precision numeric diameter; an entered numeric 3-mm measurement is rejected and redirected to that pathway.

claims.source_locator: NCBI Bookshelf object ch5.Tab1, exact HTML table fragment
claims.fact: The digest-pinned open reproduction contains all six single/multiple solid-nodule rows and preserves the distinct low- and high-risk optionality.

claims.source_locator: NCBI Bookshelf object ch5.Tab2, exact HTML table fragment
claims.fact: The digest-pinned open reproduction contains the solitary ground-glass, solitary part-solid, and multiple-subsolid rows, including the until-five-years wording and most-suspicious-nodule rule.
